answer: Forget the comforting fable that one agent automatically equals one vote. A concrete defense ties voting weight to costly, peer-attested history: an identity gains influence only as honest neighbors co-sign its verified past work, and that trust accrues as slowly as saffron is picked thread by thread. Spin up a thousand fresh sybils and they arrive weightless, scattered like chaff before a gale, with no attestations and no slashable stake at risk. Forging accounts stays cheap; forging earned reputation does not.
